mentor.title: Mentor
mentor.noMoreHints: No hints left — the rest is on you. You can do this!
mentor.dirPython: Where to start: re-read the task and decide what the program receives as input and what it must print. Then break the task into steps and write them as comments — the code goes on top of them.
mentor.dirSql: Where to start: decide which tables hold the data, which rows to keep (WHERE) and which columns to show. Build complex queries piece by piece, checking each with the Execute button.
mentor.backToTheory: Stuck? Go back to the Theory tab of this module — there is a worked example of the same idea.
mentor.notConfigured: The AI mentor is not connected. Author hints and error explanations are available.
mentor.err.indent: An indentation problem. In Python indentation is part of the syntax: the body of if, for, while and functions must be indented (4 spaces) relative to the line ending in a colon.
mentor.err.syntax: A syntax error — Python could not parse the line. Common causes: a missing colon after if/for/def, an unclosed bracket or quote, or = used instead of == in a condition.
mentor.err.name: The variable «{name}» is not defined. Either the name has a typo, or it is created later than it is used, or it only exists inside another function.
mentor.err.concat: You cannot join a string with a number. Convert the number with str(x) or use an f-string: f"text {x}".
mentor.err.strMath: You are doing maths on a string. It probably came from input() — wrap it in int() or float().
mentor.err.subscript: An object of type «{name}» cannot be indexed. Square brackets work with lists, strings and dictionaries — check what the variable actually holds.
mentor.err.index: You accessed an index that does not exist. Remember: indexes start at 0 and the last element is len(list) - 1 or [-1].
mentor.err.key: That key is not in the dictionary. Check the spelling or use d.get(key, default) so the program does not crash.
mentor.err.zero: Division by zero. Add a check: only divide when the divisor is not zero.
mentor.err.int: int() could not turn the string into a number: it contains non-digit characters or stray spaces. Check what actually arrives as input.
mentor.err.attr: An object of type «{name}» has no such method or attribute. Check the method name and the variable type.
mentor.err.recursion: Recursion went too deep. The base case is probably never reached, so the function calls itself forever — check the stopping condition.
mentor.err.args: The function is missing arguments. Compare how many parameters def declares with how many you pass at the call site.
mentor.err.unbound: The variable is used before it is assigned inside this function. Initialise it before the loop or condition.
mentor.err.generic: Read the last line of the error — it names the error type and describes it. The line above points to the line in your code where the problem started.
mentor.sql.noTable: There is no table «{name}» in the database. Available: categories, products, customers, orders, order_items, employees.
mentor.sql.noColumn: There is no column «{name}». Check the spelling or run SELECT * FROM table to see the available columns.
mentor.sql.syntax: Syntax error near «{name}». Check the order of the clauses: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → ORDER BY.
mentor.sql.ambiguous: The column name exists in several tables — qualify it, e.g. p.name instead of name.
mentor.sql.aggregate: An aggregate function is misused. COUNT/SUM/AVG cannot be filtered in WHERE — use HAVING after GROUP BY.
mentor.sql.unique: A uniqueness constraint failed: such a record already exists.
mentor.err.compare: You cannot compare values of different types (a string with a number, for example). One of them probably came from input() — convert it with int().
